q1_issues.issue: The content clause "that they really hate Islam" — the complement of "evidence" — is entirely unencoded, leaving (Name islam "Islam") as an orphan atom for a referent that appears nowhere else in the parse.
The explicative link "meaning that" between the two quoted clauses is unrecorded, so the seal reads as a bare conjunction of two unrelated propositions.
"should have" loses its strength-0.7 reading: (Obligated sk_have_1) sits inside a seal carrying one (STV 1.0 0.99), making it indistinguishable from "must have".

q2_gaps: a noun's finite that-clause complement ("authentic evidence ... that they really hate Islam") — only PP arguments of nouns are legislated, so a content clause on a noun has no encoding

a sentential explicative participle linking two clauses ("P, meaning that Q") — not in the causal / purposive / concessive / adversative connective families, and not a noun post-modifier reduced relative
per-conjunct truth values inside a seal, so a sealed "should" cannot carry strength 0.7 and a sealed deontic collapses onto the plain one
first- and second-person pronouns ("we") have no legislated referent treatment; the pronoun rules cover only he / she / it / they

a framing/domain PP scoping a copular clause ("In jihad, the target must be clear") — the framing PP needs an eventuality to attach to, but a framing PP is not one of the listed state-reification triggers
notes: Direct-quotation routing (say + Experiencer + Past, content sealed under Theme, definite target typing projected) and the have/Holder/Theme possession roles are correct. Most of the loss traces to the gaps above rather than to mis-slotting.
